import os
from collections.abc import Iterator

from sqlmodel import Session, SQLModel, create_engine

DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite:///./inventory.db")
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False} if DATABASE_URL.startswith("sqlite") else {})


def init_db() -> None:
    SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine)


def get_session() -> Iterator[Session]:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session
from sqlmodel import Field, SQLModel


class ItemBase(SQLModel):
    name: str
    price_cents: int


class Item(ItemBase, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)


class ItemCreate(ItemBase):
    pass


class ItemRead(ItemBase):
    id: int
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.db import get_session, init_db
from app.models import Item, ItemCreate, ItemRead


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    init_db()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]


@app.post("/items", response_model=ItemRead)
def create_item(item: ItemCreate, session: SessionDep) -> Item:
    db_item = Item.model_validate(item)
    session.add(db_item)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app


def test_create_item():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        r = client.post("/items", json={"name": "pen", "price_cents": 150})
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert r.json()["name"] == "pen"

### Define HeroPublicWithTeam and TeamPublicWithHeroes models

Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/fastapi/relationships.md

Adds two data models that inherit from HeroPublic and TeamPublic to include related data for single-item responses. The team field uses TeamPublic and heroes uses HeroPublic to avoid infinite recursion. These are not table models and cannot have Relationship attributes.

```python
class HeroPublicWithTeam(HeroPublic):
    team: TeamPublic | None = None


class TeamPublicWithHeroes(TeamPublic):
    heroes: list[HeroPublic] = []
```

--------------------------------

### Update path operations to use relationship models

Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/fastapi/relationships.md

Modify the read_hero and read_team path operations to use response models HeroPublicWithTeam and TeamPublicWithHeroes, so FastAPI extracts the team and heroes attributes from the returned table models.

```python
@app.get("/heroes/{hero_id}", response_model=HeroPublicWithTeam)
def read_hero(session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)], hero_id: int):
    hero = session.get(Hero, hero_id)
    if not hero:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Hero not found")
    return hero
@app.get("/teams/{team_id}", response_model=TeamPublicWithHeroes)
def read_team(team_id: int, session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]):
    team = session.get(Team, team_id)
    if not team:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Team not found")
    return team
```

--------------------------------

### SQLModel table models with relationship attributes

Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/fastapi/teams.md

Defines Team and Hero table models with Relationship() attributes for automatic data fetching. Relationship attributes are only in table models, not in base or public models. Includes TeamCreate, TeamPublic, TeamUpdate, HeroBase, HeroPublic, HeroCreate, and HeroUpdate models.

```python
class TeamBase(SQLModel):
    name: str = Field(index=True)
    headquarters: str


class Team(TeamBase, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)

    heroes: list["Hero"] = Relationship(back_populates="team")


class TeamCreate(TeamBase):
    pass


class TeamPublic(TeamBase):
    id: int


class TeamUpdate(SQLModel):
    name: str | None = None
    headquarters: str | None = None


class HeroBase(SQLModel):
    name: str = Field(index=True)
    secret_name: str
    age: int | None = Field(default=None, index=True)

    team_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="team.id")


class Hero(HeroBase, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)

    team: Team | None = Relationship(back_populates="heroes")


class HeroPublic(HeroBase):
    id: int


class HeroCreate(HeroBase):
    pass


class HeroUpdate(SQLModel):
    name: str | None = None
    secret_name: str | None = None
    age: int | None = None
    team_id: int | None = None
```

--------------------------------

### Models with Relationships in FastAPI > Why Aren't We Getting More Data

Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/fastapi/relationships.md

## Why Aren't We Getting More Data

First, why is it that we are not getting the related data for each hero and for each team?

It's because we declared the `HeroPublic` with only the same base fields of the `HeroBase` plus the `id`. But it doesn't include a field `team` for the **relationship attribute**.

And the same way, we declared the `TeamPublic` with only the same base fields of the `TeamBase` plus the `id`. But it doesn't include a field `heroes` for the **relationship attribute**.

```python
class TeamBase(SQLModel):
    name: str = Field(index=True)
    headquarters: str
class TeamPublic(TeamBase):
    id: int
class HeroBase(SQLModel):
    name: str = Field(index=True)
    secret_name: str
    age: int | None = Field(default=None, index=True)

    team_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="team.id")
class HeroPublic(HeroBase):
    id: int
```

Now, remember that [FastAPI uses the `response_model` to validate and **filter** the response data](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/)?

In this case, we used `response_model=TeamPublic` and `response_model=HeroPublic`, so FastAPI will use them to filter the response data, even if we return a **table model** that includes **relationship attributes**:

```python

    hero = session.get(Hero, hero_id)
    if not hero:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Hero not found")
    return hero
@app.get("/teams/{team_id}", response_model=TeamPublic)
def read_team(team_id: int, session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]):
    team = session.get(Team, team_id)
    if not team:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Team not found")
    return team
```

Defines Team and Hero table models with Relationship() attributes for automatic data fetching. Relationship attributes are only in table models, not in base or public models. Includes TeamCreate, TeamPublic, TeamUpdate, HeroBase, HeroPublic, HeroCreate, and HeroUpdate models.

```python
class TeamBase(SQLModel):
    name: str = Field(index=True)
    headquarters: str


class Team(TeamBase, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)

    heroes: list["Hero"] = Relationship(back_populates="team")


class TeamCreate(TeamBase):
    pass


class TeamPublic(TeamBase):
    id: int


class TeamUpdate(SQLModel):
    name: str | None = None
    headquarters: str | None = None


class HeroBase(SQLModel):

    secret_name: str
    age: int | None = Field(default=None, index=True)

    team_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="team.id")


class Hero(HeroBase, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)

    team: Team | None = Relationship(back_populates="heroes")


class HeroPublic(HeroBase):
    id: int


class HeroCreate(HeroBase):
    pass

### Models with Relationships in FastAPI > Why Aren't We Getting More Data

Source: https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/blob/main/docs/tutorial/fastapi/relationships.md

## Why Aren't We Getting More Data

First, why is it that we are not getting the related data for each hero and for each team?

It's because we declared the `HeroPublic` with only the same base fields of the `HeroBase` plus the `id`. But it doesn't include a field `team` for the **relationship attribute**.

And the same way, we declared the `TeamPublic` with only the same base fields of the `TeamBase` plus the `id`. But it doesn't include a field `heroes` for the **relationship attribute**.

```python
class TeamBase(SQLModel):
    name: str = Field(index=True)
    headquarters: str
class TeamPublic(TeamBase):
    id: int
class HeroBase(SQLModel):
    name: str = Field(index=True)
    secret_name: str
    age: int | None = Field(default=None, index=True)

    team_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="team.id")
class HeroPublic(HeroBase):
    id: int
```

Now, remember that [FastAPI uses the `response_model` to validate and **filter** the response data](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/)?

In this case, we used `response_model=TeamPublic` and `response_model=HeroPublic`, so FastAPI will use them to filter the response data, even if we return a **table model** that includes **relationship attributes**:

```python
@app.get("/heroes/{hero_id}", response_model=HeroPublic)
def read_hero(session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)], hero_id: int):
    hero = session.get(Hero, hero_id)
    if not hero:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Hero not found")
    return hero
@app.get("/teams/{team_id}", response_model=TeamPublic)
def read_team(team_id: int, session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]):
    team = session.get(Team, team_id)
    if not team:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Team not found")
    return team
```
